source: No deceptive statement is sincere. At least one statement is deceptive. Therefore at least one statement is not sincere.

claims.text: At least one statement is deceptive.

evidence.quote: At least one statement is deceptive.

translations.reason: Universal quantification with domain restriction: All deceptive statements are not sincere
Existential quantification with domain restriction: There exists at least one deceptive statement
Existential quantification with domain restriction: There exists at least one statement that is not sincere

interpretation_notes: The domain is explicitly set to 'All individuals.' with noun restrictions encoded via the Statement predicate. The universal premise now includes an explicit conjunction with Statement(x) to restrict scope. The existential claims similarly combine Statement(x) with their properties. This preserves the original meaning while conforming to the required domain normalization.
